tarjetas.p: How many bones does the skull have, and how are they divided?
tarjetas.r: 22: 8 in the neurocranium + 14 in the viscerocranium (including the mandible). Iwanaga counts 23 because he adds the hyoid.

tarjetas.p: Name the 4 unpaired bones of the neurocranium, from front to back
tarjetas.r: Frontal → ethmoid → sphenoid → occipital

tarjetas.p: Which bones of the neurocranium are paired?
tarjetas.r: Temporals and parietals

tarjetas.p: Viscerocranium: what are the 6 paired and the 2 unpaired bones?
tarjetas.r:
Paired: maxillae, zygomatics, nasals, lacrimals, palatines, inferior nasal conchae.
Unpaired: mandible and vomer.

tarjetas.p: Which nasal concha is a separate bone, and which ones belong to the ethmoid?
tarjetas.r: The inferior concha is a separate bone; the superior and middle conchae are parts of the ethmoid.

tarjetas.p: Which 4 bones form the pterion?
tarjetas.r: Frontal, parietal, greater wing of the sphenoid and temporal (H-shaped).

tarjetas.p: Which artery runs on the inner surface of the pterion, and what injury does its rupture cause?
tarjetas.r: The anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery → epidural hematoma.

tarjetas.p: Which bones does the coronal suture join?
tarjetas.r: Frontal and parietals (it does not touch the temporal).

tarjetas.p: Which bones does the squamous suture join?
tarjetas.r: Temporal and parietal.

tarjetas.p: Which bones does the metopic suture join?
tarjetas.r: The two halves of the frontal bone (at birth the frontal is two bones).

tarjetas.p: Which suture joins the temporal bone to the occipital?
tarjetas.r: The occipitomastoid suture.

tarjetas.p: Where does the coronal suture end, and why doesn't the frontal bone normally touch the temporal?
tarjetas.r: At the pterion: the greater wing of the sphenoid is in between.

tarjetas.p: Is the pterygopalatine fossa a suture?
tarjetas.r: No: it is a space (fossa) behind the maxilla.

tarjetas.p: Is the mastoid a bone?
tarjetas.r: No: it is a part of the temporal bone.

tarjetas.p: What is the bregma, and which fontanelle sits there?
tarjetas.r: The junction of the coronal and sagittal sutures. The anterior fontanelle sits there.

tarjetas.p: What is the lambda, and which fontanelle sits there?
tarjetas.r: The junction of the sagittal and lambdoid sutures. The posterior fontanelle sits there.

tarjetas.p: What shape are the anterior and posterior fontanelles, and why?
tarjetas.r:
Anterior: diamond (4 bones: 2 frontal halves + 2 parietals).
Posterior: triangle (3 bones: 2 parietals + occipital).

tarjetas.p: When do the anterior and posterior fontanelles close?
tarjetas.r: Anterior: ~18 months (highly variable). Posterior: ~3 months.

tarjetas.p: When does the metopic suture close physiologically?
tarjetas.r: During the first year: on CT, 100% are closed by 9 months (Vu 2001).

tarjetas.p: Which bones meet at the asterion?
tarjetas.r: Parietal, occipital and temporal (mastoid part).

tarjetas.p: How many fontanelles does a newborn have, and where are they?
tarjetas.r: 6: anterior (bregma), posterior (lambda), 2 anterolateral/sphenoidal (pterion) and 2 posterolateral/mastoid (asterion).

tarjetas.p: What does Virchow's law state?
tarjetas.r: When a suture fuses prematurely, growth perpendicular to it is lost and the skull compensates by growing parallel to it.

tarjetas.p: Sagittal synostosis: what shape does the skull take, and why?
tarjetas.r: Scaphocephaly (long and narrow): transverse growth is lost and the skull compensates front to back.

tarjetas.p: Metopic synostosis: what shape does the skull take, and what orbital sign does it cause?
tarjetas.r: Trigonocephaly (pointed forehead, wide parietal region) with hypotelorism. Lateral widening of the forehead is lost.

tarjetas.p: Why is an epidural hematoma biconvex?
tarjetas.r: The dura is most firmly attached to bone at the sutures, so the hematoma cannot cross them and builds up inward.

tarjetas.p: Epidural vs. subdural on CT
tarjetas.r:
Epidural: biconvex, does not cross sutures, arterial.
Subdural: crescent, crosses sutures, venous.

tarjetas.p: Why is there a lucid interval in an epidural hematoma if the bleeding is arterial?
tarjetas.r: Blood takes time to strip the adherent dura and the brain compensates at first. Once compensation is exhausted, deterioration is abrupt.

tarjetas.p: Epidural hematoma + ipsilateral mydriasis: mechanism?
tarjetas.r: Uncal herniation compressing CN III against the tentorium. The pupillary fibers run on the surface of the nerve, so mydriasis comes first.

tarjetas.p: Which 4 bones does the zygoma articulate with?
tarjetas.r: Frontal, maxilla, temporal (at the arch) and sphenoid (in the lateral orbital wall).

tarjetas.p: Which suture is the best landmark that the zygoma has been correctly reduced?
tarjetas.r: The sphenozygomatic suture, in the lateral orbital wall (Perry & Holmes, p. 149).

tarjetas.p: Anterior fontanelle: bulging vs. sunken
tarjetas.r: Bulging: raised intracranial pressure. Sunken: dehydration.

tarjetas.p: Point to the spot on the temple where 4 bones meet, and name them
tarjetas.r: Pterion: frontal, parietal, greater wing of the sphenoid and temporal (H-shaped).

tarjetas.p: Epidural or subdural? Why?
tarjetas.r: Epidural: biconvex lens that does not cross sutures (arterial, middle meningeal artery).

tarjetas.p:
Epidural or subdural? Why?
(second image)
tarjetas.r: Subdural: crescent that follows the contour of the brain and crosses sutures (venous).

tarjetas.p: Which craniosynostosis is this, and which suture fused?
tarjetas.r: Trigonocephaly from metopic synostosis (keel-shaped forehead; look for hypotelorism).

tarjetas.p:
Which craniosynostosis is this, and which suture fused?
(3D skull)
tarjetas.r: Scaphocephaly from sagittal synostosis (long, narrow skull).
